#Pyspark #Sql #AzureDataEngineer #InterviewQuestions 
#PalTech : Write a Pyspark and SQL code to count the number of certificates to be paid from a Certificates table, where each candidate (Name) can have at most two active certificates at any time. A certificate is active from DateofCertification to DateOfExpiry (inclusive of start month, exclusive of end month). If a third certificate is active concurrently, it is not paid.

Table has schema like:
 CertificateId int,
 Name string, 
 DateofCertification string, 
 DateOfExpiry string

Date like:
INSERT INTO Certificates (CertificateId, Name, DateofCertification, DateOfExpiry) VALUES
(1, 'a', 'Nov 2024', 'Mar 2025'), -- Active Nov - Mar 2024
(2, 'a', 'Dec 2024', 'Feb 2025'), -- Active Dec 2024
(3, 'a', 'Jan 2025', 'Mar 2025'), -- Inactive
(3, 'a', 'Feb 2025', 'Mar 2025'), -- Inactive
(4, 'a', 'Apr 2025', 'May 2025'), -- Active Apr 2025
(5, 'b', 'May 2024', 'Dec 2024'), -- Active May-Dec 2024
(6, 'b', 'Oct 2024', 'Feb 2025'), -- Active Oct2024 - Feb 2025
(7, 'b', 'Nov 2024', 'Mar 2025'), -- Inactive
(8, 'c', 'Jan 2024', 'Apr 2024'), -- Active Jan-Apr 2024
(9, 'c', 'Mar 2024', 'Jun 2024'); -- Active Mar-Jun 2024

will be posting both the solutions in comments.
…see more

ai_analysis.summary: An incomplete interview prompt asks for PySpark and SQL code to count paid certificates per candidate when each candidate may have at most two concurrently active certificates. A certificate is active from its certification month inclusively to its expiry month exclusively. The post provides a schema and sample records, but it does not include the promised solutions, specify which certificates to pay when more than two overlap, or explain why CertificateId 3 appears twice. One comment also appears inconsistent with the stored dates by describing certificate 1 as ending in Mar 2024 rather than Mar 2025.
subtopics: Ambiguous selection when more than two certificates overlap

interview_questions.question: How would you write PySpark and SQL logic to count the certificates that should be paid for each candidate under the two-active-certificate limit?
interview_questions.answer:
The logic treats DateofCertification as inclusive and DateOfExpiry as exclusive.
The logic evaluates overlapping certificates separately for each candidate name.
The logic handles the month-year values stored as strings consistently.
The answer recognizes that the post does not define which certificates to select when more than two overlap.

interview_questions.question: Under the stated date rule, when are two certificates for the same candidate considered concurrent?
interview_questions.answer:
A certificate is active in its certification month but not in its expiry month.
Two certificates for the same candidate are concurrent when their half-open active intervals overlap.
For example, the January-to-April and March-to-June intervals for candidate c overlap during March.

interview_questions.question: What ambiguities in the supplied statement must be resolved before claiming that the paid-certificate result is uniquely correct?
interview_questions.answer:
No rule identifies which two certificates to pay when a candidate has more than two active certificates.
CertificateId 3 is repeated without an explanation of whether the rows are distinct certificates or duplicate data.
The comment for certificate 1 gives Mar 2024 as its end, while its DateOfExpiry value is Mar 2025.
